newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Strikes cost S.Korea $2.14 bln in lost output.
newsitem.headline: Strikes cost S.Korea $2.14 bln in lost output.

text.p: Recent nationwide labour strikes have cost South Korea an estimated 1.81 trillion won ($2.14 billion) in lost production as of 10.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Saturday, a trade ministry official said.
Lost exports from the start of industrial action on December 26 were estimated at $345 million, he said.
The biggest losses were in the country's automobile industry, which posted 1.45 trillion won ($1.7 billion) in production losses and $222 million in export losses, the official said.

South Korea's major industries have been crippled by strikes in protest at the passage of a new labour law, which allows employers to lay off workers, replace strikers and implement flexible work hours.
